subject: Route economics investigation checklist & fallthrough policy
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Route economics investigation checklist & fallthrough policy

Team —

Following the spike we saw last week where a handful of routes started showing 3x unit-cost while latency stayed flat, I want to formalize a short investigation checklist and an explicit fallthrough policy we can ship into Console quick. Goal: reduce manual triage time and prevent noisy Billing/CS escalations.

Top-level asks:
- Can Eng own a single triage checklist document we can iterate on? (see attached sample)
- Product: define acceptance criteria for the console tile that links cost anomalies to topology/trace and suggests fallback models.
- Observability: propose minimal telemetry additions (sampling, KV-cache hit metrics, per-model-variant token buckets) that let us explain cost deltas.

Constraints: minimal infra changes for Q1; UX should be usable by CS and SEs without requiring infra tickets.

I've attached a CSV sample from the Acme spike and a triage-checklist template. Also: draft design in Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-route-econ-design and I've opened JIRA OBS-1427.

Expecting short replies with owners + rough E2E estimate (low/med/high) by EOD.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Product Observability
Redwood Inference

--- Attachment stubs: route-econ-sample.csv (csv, 120KB), triage-checklist-template.md (md, 8KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Route economics investigation checklist & fallthrough policy

Sofia —

Thanks for the clear ask. Quick responses inline: 

- Triage doc owner: happy to own the checklist and iterate with Eng/Obs. I'll convert your template into a living doc and share. (Estimate: low effort to create, medium to stabilize with examples.)
- Console tile: acceptance criteria I'd propose:
  * Tile shows 24h cost delta and per-token delta (absolute + pct) for the selected route slice.
  * Link out to sample traces (top 3 traces by token cost) and model variant breakdown.
  * One-click suggest: fallback to cheaper variant or apply cached prefix if available.
  * Guardrails: only show suggestions when historical quality delta below threshold (TBD).

Questions for Eng/Obs: what minimal telemetry do you need to make "one-click suggest" actionable? I want the first iteration to be read-only, then add actions in v1.1.

I'll own UX copy and PM signoff. Rough effort: medium.

— Marissa
PM, Observability

> On Mon, 16 Nov 2026 at 09:12, Sofia Ivanova wrote:
> > Team —
> > Following the spike we saw last week...

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Route economics investigation checklist & fallthrough policy

Sofia / Marissa —

Thanks. Technical notes / constraints from Observability infra: 

- Sampling: we can add a lightweight high-cost-sample that captures full request/response + trace for up to 0.1% of tokens per route. That should be enough to surface expensive paths without big storage delta. Low effort (low).
- KV-cache hitmetrics: we can surface per-route cache hit ratio and avg tokens saved, but this requires tagging at the routing layer (small schema change). Medium effort.
- Per-variant accounting: we already emit model_variant IDs in logs but not aggregated per-route per-hour. We can backfill recent 30d via offline job and ship hourly aggregates. Medium-high.

Regarding "one-click suggest" — please note: we cannot auto-apply model fallbacks without a manual approval flow (safety/QA). We can provide a suggested button that opens a lightweight runbook for SE/CS to apply via Console.

I'll add concrete telemetry fields to OBS-1427. Attaching a quick CSV with the sample spike mapping into the metrics fields you asked for.

— Ben
Senior Observability Engineer

--- Attachment stubs: route-econ-sample.csv (csv, 120KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 12:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Route economics investigation checklist & fallthrough policy

Sofia / team —

Great start. A few items to fold into the checklist and acceptance criteria: 

- CS playbook snippet: what screenshots / links should we show to an account manager when an alert fires? Add to triage doc.
- SLA exceptions: define when we escalate to Eng (e.g., >5% of routes exceed x unit-cost for 6h).
- Canary policy: for any suggested fallback, require a 24h canary limited to 5% of traffic + automated quality regression monitor (prompt set).
- Rollback policy: auto-rollback if quality regression or error-rate increase > 0.5% vs baseline.

I'll draft the CS playbook and acceptance test checklist — estimate: low.

Irene Choi
Head of Customer Success (observability customers)

Subject: Re: Route economics investigation checklist & fallthrough policy

Thanks all — solid alignment. Action items: 

1) Marissa: own triage checklist doc + UX acceptance criteria. Share first draft by Wed EOD (low effort).
2) Ben: add telemetry fields to OBS-1427 and prototype the 0.1% high-cost sampling job. Estimate: medium.
3) Irene: draft CS playbook + screenshots; wire in SLA thresholds (low).
4) Sofia: coordinate with Legal on any UI language that looks like "suggested fallback" (I will ping Legal).

I'll create a short Slack channel (#route-econ) and drop links. If we agree, target a read-only Console tile in the 1.7 sprint and actioning UX in 1.8.

Closing note: prioritize conservative defaults for automated suggestions — we want humans in the loop for now.

Sofia
Director, Product Observability
Redwood Inference

Onward —
